item.title: Legal Core
item.lead: This concluding page summarizes the editorial stance without presenting the source claims as independently proven facts.

items: The source primarily identifies blind spots at the intersection of privacy, consumer law, contracts, and platform responsibility.
Transparency regarding identity and automation is central.
The Lex Humanitas Digitalis comprises four proposed pillars: transparency, data minimization, chain liability, and financial audit.
Feasibility depends on clear definitions, rights to evidence, and cross-border enforcement.

blocks.label: SOURCE STATUS
blocks.text: Based on the sections concerning legal evidence, consumer protection, GDPR, jurisdictional opportunism, and the proposed Lex Humanitas Digitalis in the provided dossier. This Research Edition 4.0 adds current public source verification as of September 19, 2026, and explicitly marks which figures/claims from the source material have not been independently verified.

Reading guide for further research. The source itself mentions legal documentation, technical data, and sociological analysis as three tracks for triangulation. In this edition, these tracks have been brought together as an editorial structure; they have not been externally verified.
